record.paper_title: KAM theorems and open problems for infinite dimensional Hamiltonian with short range
record.original_question: Consider a Hamiltonian system whose linearized operator, for example -Delta_f + v, has continuous spectrum consisting of an interval. Can the system have KAM tori, even when the Hamiltonian itself may be short range?

evidence.quote: Remark 3. We have seen that the pure point spectra property is of key importance for the existence of quasi-periodic breathers for Hamiltonian with short range. If W(x) = 1/2 x^2 + ..., the linearized system of (2.6) is of continuous spectra which is the whole of the interval [beta,beta +1].

Problem 3. Assume that the linearized operator (-Delta_f + v, for example,) of a hamiltonian system contains continuous spectra which consist of an interval. Are there any KAM tori for the system? even if the system may be of short range. In general, the answer trends to be no.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system on a suitable phase space whose linearization at an equilibrium is a self-adjoint operator of the form $L = -\Delta_f + v$ (for instance, a discrete Laplacian on a lattice plus a multiplication/potential term, or a Schrödinger-type operator) with the property that the spectrum of $L$ contains an interval of continuous spectrum. The full Hamiltonian is assumed to have short-range interactions, meaning that the coupling between sites (or between Fourier/eigen-modes) decays sufficiently fast (e.g., exponentially or with sufficient polynomial rate) with respect to the distance between indices.

A KAM torus is, in this setting, a finite- or infinite-dimensional invariant torus on which the flow is conjugate to a Diophantine linear flow, persisting under the nonlinear perturbation.

Question: Under these hypotheses, can such a Hamiltonian system possess KAM tori? In other words, is it possible to establish (or to rule out) the existence of quasi-periodic invariant tori for short-range Hamiltonian systems whose linearized operator has continuous spectrum forming an interval?
artifact.category_tag: KAM theory for infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems
artifact.status_search_result: Literature on infinite-dimensional KAM theory with short-range couplings (e.g., Pöschel-type results, and follow-up work on Kolmogorov-type theorems for short-range Hamiltonian systems) consistently assumes pure point spectrum of the linearized operator. No published result was found establishing KAM tori when the linearized operator has continuous spectrum forming an interval; the question is generally expected to have a negative answer but appears unresolved in the affirmative or definitive negative direction.

status_evidence.title: On the Kolmogorov theorem for some infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems of short range
status_evidence.snippet: Extension of Kolmogorov theorem to infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems with short-range couplings, assuming pure point spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Existing short-range KAM results assume pure point spectrum, not continuous spectrum.

status_evidence.title: Maximal tori in infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems: a Renormalization Group approach
status_evidence.snippet: Renormalization Group approach to maximal tori in infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems with short-range couplings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to focus on short-range systems with discrete spectrum; continuous-spectrum case not addressed.
